territorial_scope.description: Applies to advertisements and election communications concerning elections in California, California candidates, elected and elections officials, and California ballot measures.

evidence.quote: in connection with an election in California

summary.short: Adds Elections Code § 20012 barring knowing, malicious distribution of materially deceptive audio or visual content (deepfakes) about California candidates, election officials and voting equipment within set periods before elections, unless labelled; allows injunctions and damages. Urgency statute, immediate effect.
summary.long: Adds Elections Code § 20012 (Sec. 3). From 120 days before a California election, and for content about elections officials and voting equipment through 60 days after, a person, committee or other entity may not knowingly and with malice distribute an advertisement or other election communication with materially deceptive audio or visual content depicting a candidate, elections official, elected official, or voting equipment. Exceptions apply where a 'This ____ has been manipulated' disclosure is included, for satire or parody with a labelled disclosure, and for certain broadcasting stations, newspapers and interactive computer services. Removing required disclosures is prohibited. Recipients, candidates, committees and elections officials may seek injunctions with attorney's fees, or damages, on clear and convincing evidence. Sections 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.5 amend Code of Civil Procedure § 35 to give election-related actions precedence, in versions that depend on Assembly Bill 2655. Sec. 6 declares an urgency statute effective immediately.

notes: The registry status 'repealed' does not appear in the document. The text contains no repeal of this act and no repeal date for Elections Code § 20012. The only sunset is in CCP § 35(b): Secs. 1 and 1.5 remain in effect only until January 1, 2027; Secs. 2 and 2.5 become operative January 1, 2027. The four versions of CCP § 35 are internally inconsistent: they list different Elections Code sections and differ in operative terms, and Secs. 4 and 5 select among them depending on AB 2655. Sec. 6 declares an urgency statute with immediate effect, although Secs. 2 and 2.5 are operative only from January 1, 2027. The document gives no enacting chapter number.

“Advertisement” means any general or public communication that is authorized or paid for the purpose of supporting or opposing a candidate for elective office in California or a ballot measure that appears on a ballot issued in California
“Broadcasting station” means a radio or television broadcasting station, including any of the following:
“Committee” means a committee as defined in Section 82013 of the Government Code.

“Deepfake” means audio or visual media that is digitally created or modified such that it would falsely appear to a reasonable person to be an authentic record of the actual speech or conduct of the individual depicted in the media.
“Election communication” means any general or public communication not covered under “advertisement”
“Elections official” means any of the following persons, but only in their capacity as a person charged with holding or conducting an election
“Malice” means the person, committee, or other entity distributed the audio or visual media knowing the materially deceptive content was false or with a reckless disregard for the truth.

“Materially deceptive content” means audio or visual media that is intentionally digitally created or modified, which includes, but is not limited to, deepfakes, such that the content would falsely appear to a reasonable person to be an authentic record of the content depicted in the media.
“Recipient” includes a person who views, hears, or otherwise perceives an image or audio or video file that was initially distributed in violation of this section.

obligations.summary: A person, committee or other entity may not, during the period in subdivision (c), with malice and knowingly, distribute an advertisement or other election communication containing materially deceptive content of the listed kinds. Under (b)(4), it may also not remove a required disclosure or knowingly republish covered content without the required disclosure.
obligations.applies_from: 120 days before any election in California (subd. (c)(1)); for items in (b)(1)(B) and (D), 120 days before through 60 days after the election (subd. (c)(2))
obligations.conditional_on: Malice and knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard; content reasonably likely to harm a candidate's reputation or prospects or falsely undermine confidence in an election outcome, depending on the category; exemptions in (b)(2), (b)(3) and (e)

evidence.quote: A person, committee, or other entity shall not, during the time period set forth in subdivision (c), with malice, knowingly distribute an advertisement or other election communication containing materially deceptive content of any of the following:

obligations.summary: Where a candidate portrays themself in covered content, or where content is satire or parody, the content must carry a disclosure reading "This ____ has been manipulated." (or "for purposes of satire or parody"), with the blank filled by Image, Audio or Video. Visual disclosures must meet size requirements, and audio disclosures must be read aloud at the beginning, end and at intervals of no more than two minutes. Under (g), the disclosure must be in the language used if that language is not English.
obligations.conditional_on: Applies only where the disclosure exemption in (b)(2) or the satire or parody exemption in (b)(3) is relied on; the time periods in subdivision (c) apply

evidence.quote: the content includes a disclosure stating “This ____ has been manipulated.”
